title: Remove default admin user and create one with other name
description: Before deploying any new Fortinet, it is important to change the password of the default admin account. It is also recommended that you change even the user name of the default admin account. However, since you cannot change the user name of an account that is currently in use, a second administrator account must be created in order to do this. FAILs if the default 'admin' account still exists. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6.1.2 Remove default admin user and create one with other name

remediation.command:
config system admin
    edit "mycompanyadmin"
        set accprofile "super_admin"
        set password <password>
    next
end
(log in as mycompanyadmin, then)
config system admin
    delete "admin"
end
# CIS guidance:
First create another local admin account, for example mycompanyadmin.
config system admin
    edit "mycompanyadmin"
        set accprofile "tier_1"
        set password ......
        set accprofile "super_admin"
    end
Verify if the newly created login works by opening another CLI session, do not logout of your current session. Once validated, logout with the default local admin account and use the CLI session with mycompanyadmin to delete the default local admin account. Please make sure there are no references in the configuration to the account (groups, etc.)
config system admin
    delete "admin"
end
To change the default password in the GUI:
System > Admin > Administrators and click on "Edit" under the "admin" user. Create New admin account (mycompanyadmin):
System > Admin > Administrators and clicking on "Add Administrator". Verify if you can login with that account via another browser session (eg. incognito mode). Remove default admin user:
System > Admin > Administrators and selecting "admin" and clicking on the "Delete" button.

title: Ensure administrator password retries and lockout time are configured
description: Failed login attempts can indicate malicious attempts to gain access to your network. To prevent this security risk, FortiSwitch is preconfigured to limit the number of failed administrator login attempts. After the maximum number of failed login attempts is reached, access to the account is blocked for the configured lockout period. PASS requires admin-lockout-threshold of 3 or less and admin-lockout-duration of 900 seconds or less, exactly as the CIS audit states (the CIS remediation value is 900). Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.1 Ensure administrator password retries and lockout time are configured

remediation.command:
config system global
    set admin-lockout-threshold 3
    set admin-lockout-duration 900
end
# CIS guidance:
To configure the lockout options, from CLI:
config system global
    set admin-lockout-threshold 3
    set admin-lockout-duration 900
end
Lockout affects the offending IP address, not the entire account.

title: Ensure management GUI listens on secure TLS version
description: As we move towards better encryption capabilities, we need to also ensure GUI access is properly secured. TLS 1.3 is currently the most secure SSL/TLS supported version for SSL-encrypted administrator access (at this time of writing). PASS requires https-ssl-versions to be exactly tlsv1-3 in config system web. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.1 Ensure management GUI listens on secure TLS version

remediation.command:
config system web
    set https-ssl-versions tlsv1-3
end
# CIS guidance:
CLI:
config system web
    set https-ssl-versions tlsv1-3
end

title: Ensure 'Password Policy' is enabled
description: It is important to use secure and complex passwords for preventing unauthorized access to the FortiSwitch device. PASS requires the password policy enabled, applied to admin-password and minimum-length 14 or more (the CIS remediation value). Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3.1 Ensure 'Password Policy' is enabled

remediation.command:
config system password-policy
    set status enable
    set apply-to admin-password ipsec-preshared-key
    set minimum-length 14
end
# CIS guidance:
Can be modified from CLI. From CLI, do the following:
config system password-policy
    set status enable
    set apply-to admin-password ipsec-preshared-key
    set minimum-length 14
end

title: Ensure only encrypted access channels are enabled
description: Allow only HTTPS access to the GUI and SSH access to the CLI. FAILs if any interface allowaccess list contains http or telnet. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4.2.2 Ensure only encrypted access channels are enabled

remediation.command:
config system interface
    edit "mgmt"
        set allowaccess https ping ssh snmp
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
If HTTP or Telnet is in the allowaccess list, you will have to set that list again with the same elements except for http or telnet. On CLI:
config system interface
    edit port1
        set allowaccess ssh https ping snmp
    end
In the web GUI, click on:
1. Network > Interfaces, select the interface and click "Edit".
2. In the interface setting page, uncheck HTTP and Telnet in the section "Administrative Access".

title: Ensure only SNMPv3 is enabled
description: Ensuring that only SNMPv3 service is enabled and SNMPv1, SNMPv2c are disabled. PASS requires the SNMP agent enabled, an empty config system snmp community block and at least one SNMPv3 user. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5.1.1 Ensure only SNMPv3 is enabled

audit.pattern:
(?ms)^config system snmp sysinfo
(?:[ 	]+[^
]*
)*?[ 	]+set status enable[ 	]*
.*?^config system snmp community
end[ 	]*$.*?^config system snmp user
[ 	]+edit

remediation.command:
config system snmp sysinfo
    set status enable
end
config system snmp community
    delete <id>
end
config system snmp user
    edit "snmp_v3"
        set security-level auth-priv
        set auth-proto sha256
        set auth-pwd <password>
        set priv-proto aes256
        set priv-pwd <password>
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
To enable SNMP agent in CLI:
config system snmp sysinfo
    set status enable
end
In GUI, go to System > Config > SNMP > Settings and enable SNMP Agent. To delete SNMPv1/2c communities. In this example, we'll delete community "public" in CLI:
First, to identify the community, run
config system snmp community
    show
    config system snmp community
        edit 1
            set name "public"
            config hosts
                edit 1
                next
            end
        next
    end
This shows that the community public has ID 1
config system snmp community
    delete 1
end
In the GUI, go to:
System > Config > SNMP > Communities, select the community and click on the Delete button. To add SNMPv3 user in CLI:
config system snmp user
    edit "snmp_test"
        set security-level auth-priv
        set auth-proto sha256
        set auth-pwd xxxx
        set priv-proto aes256
        set priv_pwd xxxx
    end
In the GUI, go to:
1. System > Config > SNMP > Users, under SNMPv3, click on "Add User" button.
2. Fill in the "Username" field.
3. Assign "SNMP Notify" hosts by clicking on the "+" button.
4. Set the "Security Level" to "Authentication and Privacy".
5. For "Authentication" choose SHA512 as Authentication Protocol.
6. Create a "Password" in the password field.
7. For "Privacy", choose AES256 as Encryption Protocol.
8. Create a "Password" in the password field.
9. Click "Add" to add the new user.

title: Allow only trusted hosts in SNMPv3
description: Ensuring that only certain hosts are able to conduct SNMP GET or receive SNMP Trap. FAILs if any SNMPv3 user lists 0.0.0.0 in notify-hosts. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5.1.2 Allow only trusted hosts in SNMPv3

remediation.command:
config system snmp user
    edit "<user>"
        set notify-hosts <nms-ip>
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
To remove 0.0.0.0 from trusted hosts in CLI:
config system snmp user
    edit "snmp_test"
        unset notify-hosts
    end
From GUI:
1. System > Config > SNMP > Users.
2. On the Users section click "Edit" on "snmp_test".
3. Remove 0.0.0.0 from "Notify Hosts" section.

title: Disable SNMPv3 Query Per User
description: Disabling SNMP query for SNMPv3 Users that only need to receive SNMP traps FAILs if any SNMPv3 user has set queries enable. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5.1.3 Disable SNMPv3 Query Per User

remediation.command:
config system snmp user
    edit "<user>"
        set queries disable
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
To disable Queries for a specific SNMPv3 User in CLI:
{snmp_test is the example SNMPv3 username}
config system snmp user
    edit snmp_test
        set queries disable
    next
end
To disable Queries for a specific SNMPv3 User in GUI:
1. System > Config > SNMP > Users
2. On the Users section click "Edit" on "snmp_test" and validate the configured SNMPv3 settings
3. Under the "Queries" section click the checkbox "Enabled" so it is turned off

title: Ensure the latest firmware is installed
description: Check against the Fortinet website to make sure that the latest stable firmware is installed.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5.2.1 Ensure the latest firmware is installed

audit.command: First, check for the latest firmware version available going to https://support.fortinet.com and login. Go to Support -> Firmware Download. Select your product and click on Download for the latest available versions. Second, verify the current firmware on your system. In the CLI: get system status ... Version: FortiSwitch-108F v7.4.6,build0895,250129 (GA) ... In the GUI: 1. Go to System > Config > Firmware 2. Check the Current Running Firmware. At the same time, go to https://www.fortiguard.com/psirt?product=FortiSwitch and check for vulnerabilities that your existing version might have.

remediation.command:
Download the required FortiSwitchOS firmware/s. Go to https://support.fortinet.com and login. Go to Support -> Firmware Download. Once there select the product. Check the latest firmware version available and choose the firmware for your specific model of the hardware. Click on "HTTPS" and "Checksum" next to your model to download the code and checksum. The last step is to install the new firmware. It is recommended to use GUI to perform this task as it would be much easier. In the GUI
1. Go to System > Config > Firmware
2. Under Upgrade File click on Choose File...
3. Then click on "Apply".

title: Enable Global Strong Encryption
description: Enable FortiSwitchOS to only use strong encryption and allow only strong ciphers for communication PASS requires set strong-crypto enable. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5.5.1 Enable Global Strong Encryption

remediation.command:
config system global
    set strong-crypto enable
end
# CIS guidance:
CLI:
config system global
    set strong-crypto enable
end

title: Ensure all the login accounts having specific trusted hosts enabled
description: Configure an administrative account to be accessible only to someone who is using a trusted host. You can set a specific IP address for the trusted host or use a subnet. FAILs if any administrator still has the default trusthost1 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6.1.1 Ensure all the login accounts having specific trusted hosts enabled

remediation.command:
config system admin
    edit "<admin>"
        set trusthost1 10.0.0.0 255.255.255.0
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
To remove a trusted host item from the list in CLI:
config system admin
    edit "test_admin"
        unset trusthost1
    end
To add a trusted host into the list in CLI:
config system admin
    edit "test_admin"
        set trusthost6 1.1.1.1 255.255.255.255
    end
Before adding an item, please make sure that it does not already exist. For example, if trusthost3 is already in the list, using it again will override the existing host/network. In the Web GUI:
1. System > Admin > Administrators.
2. Select the account "test_admin" and click on "Edit".
3. In the account setting page, make sure that "Restrict this Admin Login from Trusted Hosts Only" is enabled and all the allowed hosts / subnets are in the list of trusted hosts.

title: Ensure all the login accounts having specific trusted hosts enabled
description: Configure an administrative account to be accessible only to someone who is using a trusted host. You can set a specific IP address for the trusted host or use a subnet. FAILs if any administrator still has the default trusthost1 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7.1.1.2 Ensure all the login accounts having specific trusted hosts enabled

remediation.command:
config system admin
    edit "<admin>"
        set trusthost1 10.0.0.0 255.255.255.0
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
To remove a trusted host item from the list in CLI:
config system admin
    edit "test_admin"
        unset trusthost1
    end
To add a trusted host into the list in CLI:
config system admin
    edit "test_admin"
        set trusthost6 1.1.1.1 255.255.255.255
    end
Before adding an item, please make sure that it does not already exist. For example, if trusthost3 is already in the list, using it again will override the existing host/network. In the Web GUI:
1. System > Administrators.
2. select the account and click on edit.
3. In the account setting page, make sure that "Restrict login to trusted hosts" is enabled and all the allowed hosts / subnets are in the list of trusted host. Please take note that certain versions of FortiOS will only show the first 3 trusted hosts in the list. If you want to see more, you have to click on the "+" sign as if you're adding a new item into the list. Keep clicking until you see an empty field of trusted host. That's when you know that you have reached the bottom of the list. To add another trusted host, fill in the empty field of the new "Trusted Host". To remove a trusted host, simply erase everything in the field of that corresponding host.

title: Ensure only encrypted access channels are enabled
description: Allow only HTTPS access to the GUI and SSH access to the CLI. FAILs if any interface allowaccess list contains http or telnet. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7.1.1.5 Ensure only encrypted access channels are enabled

remediation.command:
config system interface
    edit "mgmt"
        set allowaccess https ping ssh snmp
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
If HTTP or Telnet is in the allowaccess list, you will have to set that list again with the same elements except for http or telnet. On CLI:
config system interface
    edit port1
        set allowaccess ssh https ping snmp
    end
In the web GUI, click on:
1. Network > Interfaces, select the interface and click "Edit".
2. In the interface setting page, uncheck HTTP and Telnet in the section "Administrative Access".

title: Dynamic ARP Inspection
description: Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) is a security feature available on switches that validates ARP packets on the network to prevent ARP spoofing and ARP-based man-in-the- middle attacks. It verifies ARP requests and responses against trusted sources, such as DHCP snooping and static ARP entries. PASS requires arp-inspection enable on at least one VLAN; confirm all user VLANs. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.5.2 Dynamic ARP Inspection

remediation.command:
config switch vlan
    edit <vlan-id>
        set arp-inspection enable
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
Following command enables Dynamic ARP inspection on the current VLAN, which means that ARP packets received from untrusted interfaces are discarded if they have an Invalid IP-to-MAC address binding. From the CLI:
config switch vlan
    edit <vlan-id>
        set arp-inspection enable
    end
From the GUI:
1. Switch > VLAN > Select a VLAN > Edit
2. Under the DHCP Snooping section check the checkbox for "Dynamic ARP Inspection". By default, all ports are untrusted so you will need to specify trusted ports for uplinks to DHCP Servers or to a directly connected DHCP Server. Refer to the DHCP Snooping section for the DHCP snooping configuration.

title: Encrypt Log Transmission to Syslog
description: Enable encryption for logs that are sent to a SIEM, FortiAnalyzer, or FortiManager. PASS requires syslog mode reliable and enc-algorithm high in config log syslogd setting. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.3.1 Encrypt Log Transmission to Syslog

remediation.command:
config log syslogd setting
    set mode reliable
    set enc-algorithm high
end
# CIS guidance:
Secure log transfer settings can only be configured on CLI:
config log syslogd setting
    set mode reliable
    set enc-algorithm high
end

title: Disable unsecure management services on Management, SVI, or Loopback interfaces
description: Only secure management related services such as HTTPS, PING, SSH, SNMP, and RADIUS should be used on management interfaces. FAILs if any interface allowaccess list contains http or telnet. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4.2.1 Disable unsecure management services on Management, SVI, or Loopback interfaces

remediation.command:
config system interface
    edit "mgmt"
        set allowaccess https ping ssh snmp
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
On GUI:
Go to "System" > "Network" > "Interface". Review the Physical, VLAN, or Loopback interface and disable HTTP and Telnet services. On CLI:
config system interface
    edit "mgmt"
        set allowaccess https ping ssh snmp
Note:
1. Interface name may differ based on deployment. For this example, mgmt is a switch with a dedicated management interface. Switches without a management interface this would be set to "internal".

title: Ensure correct system time is configured through NTP
description: You can either manually set the FortiSwitchOS system time, or configure the device to automatically keep its system time correct by synchronizing with a Network Time Protocol (NTP) server. These settings enable the use of primary and secondary NTP servers to provide redundancy in case of a failure involving the primary NTP server. PASS requires ntpsync enable in config system ntp; confirm synchronisation with 'diag sys ntp status'. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5.4.1 Ensure correct system time is configured through NTP

remediation.command:
config system ntp
    set ntpsync enable
    config ntpserver
        edit 1
            set server "pool.ntp.org"
        next
        edit 2
            set server "1.1.1.1"
        next
    end
end
# CIS guidance:
Only one NTP server allowed in the GUI. 'System' > 'Config' > 'Time'. Use CLI to configure additional NTP Servers. In this example, we'll assign pool.ntp.org as primary NTP server and 1.1.1.1 as secondary NTP server.
config system ntp
    config ntpserver
        edit 1
            set server pool.ntp.org
        next
        edit 2
            set server 1.1.1.1
        end
    end

title: Ensure admin accounts with different privileges have their correct profiles assigned
description: Verify that users with access to the Fortinet should only have the minimum privileges required for that particular user.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6.2.1 Ensure admin accounts with different privileges have their correct profiles assigned

audit.command: Run 'show full-configuration system accprofile' and review each admin profile: privileges (admingrp, loggrp, netgrp, sysgrp, swcoregrp, ...) must match the role. Then 'show full-configuration system admin' and confirm every administrator's accprofile matches their role (least privilege).

remediation.command:
In this example, the goal is to provide the profile "tier_1" the ability to read only. In CLI:
config system accprofile
    edit "tier_1"
        set admingrp read
        set exec-alias-grp read
        set loggrp read
        set mntgrp read
        set netgrp read
        set pktmongrp read
        set routegrp read
        set swcoregrp read
        set swmonguardgrp read
        set sysgrp read
        set utilgrp read
    end
For the GUI, go to:
1. System > Admin > Profiles, select "tier_1" and click "Edit".
2. Click on "Read Only" option for all "Access Control" privileges.
3. Click on "Update". In the next example, assign the profile "tier_1" to the account "support1". In the CLI:
config system admin
    edit "support1"
        set accprofile "tier_1"
    end
For the GUI, go to:
1. System > Admin > Administrators.
2. Select "support1" and click "Edit".
3. Under "Admin Profile", select "tier_1".

title: Ensure default Admin ports are changed
description: FortiSwitch admin ports listen on the common ports of 80 and 443. This is default behavior. While interface access is controlled by configuring network interfaces, the FortiSwitch still listens on the admin ports that have been configured, which can also cause a conflict should 80 or 443 be needed as part of additional configuration later on. FAILs if the SSH admin port is still 22 or the HTTPS admin port is still 443. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6.3.1 Ensure default Admin ports are changed

remediation.command:
config system global
    set admin-ssh-port 4422
end
config system web
    set https-port 4443
end
# CIS guidance:
CLI for changing SSH port:
config system global
    set admin-ssh-port 4422 **(or any other uncommon port)**
end
CLI for changing HTTPS port:
config system web
    set https-port 4443 **(or any other uncommon port)**
end
OR From Web GUI:
1. System > Admin > Settings
2. Change the ports/settings under 'Console Access' and 'Web Interface' sections.

title: Ensure Admin idle timeout time is configured
description: The idle timeout period is the amount of time that an administrator will stay logged in to the GUI without any activity. PASS requires admintimeout between 1 and 5 minutes. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6.3.2 Ensure Admin idle timeout time is configured

remediation.command:
config system global
    set admintimeout 5
end
# CIS guidance:
To change the idle timeout in the GUI:
1) Login to FortiSwitch with Super Admin privileges.
2) Go to 'System' > 'Admin' > 'Settings'.
3) In the 'Administration Settings' section, set the 'Idle Timeout' value to five minutes by typing 5.
4) Click 'Update'. To change the idle timeout in the CLI:
config system global
    set admintimeout 5
end

title: Ensure admin accounts with different privileges have their correct profiles assigned
description: Verify that users with access to the Fortinet should only have the minimum privileges required for that particular user.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7.1.1.3 Ensure admin accounts with different privileges have their correct profiles assigned

audit.command: Run 'show full-configuration system accprofile' and review each admin profile: privileges must match the role, with custom sub-permissions checked. Then 'show full-configuration system admin' and confirm every administrator's accprofile matches their role (least privilege).

remediation.command:
In this example, the goal is to provide the profile "tier_1" the ability to view and modify address objects. This sub-privilege is under fwgrp privilege. In CLI:
config system accprofile
    edit "tier_1"
        set fwgrp custom
        config fwgrp-permission
            set address read-write
        end
    end
For the GUI, go to:
1. System > Admin Profiles, select "tier_1" and click "Edit".
2. On "Firewall", click on "Custom".
3. Click on "Read/Write" option for "Address". In the next example, assign the profile "tier_1" to the account "support1". In the CLI:
config system admin
    edit "support1"
        set accprofile "tier_1"
    end
For the GUI, go to:
1. System > Administrators.
2. Select "support1" and click "Edit".
3. Under "Administrator Profile", select "tier_1".

title: Ensure Admin idle timeout time is configured
description: The idle timeout period is the amount of time that an administrator will stay logged in to the GUI without any activity. PASS requires admintimeout between 1 and 5 minutes. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7.1.1.4 Ensure Admin idle timeout time is configured

remediation.command:
config system global
    set admintimeout 5
end
# CIS guidance:
To change the idle timeout in the GUI:
1) Login to FortiGate with Super Admin privileges
2) Go to 'System' > 'Settings'.
3) In the 'Administration Settings' section, set the 'Idle timeout' value to five minutes by typing 5.
4) Click Apply. To change the idle timeout in the CLI:
config system global
    set admintimeout 5
end

title: Apply Local-in Policies
description: Configure Local-in Policies to control inbound traffic that is destined to a FortiGate interface. PASS requires at least one local-in policy. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7.1.1.6 Apply Local-in Policies

remediation.command:
Local-in Policies can only be configured through the CLI:
config firewall {local-in-policy | local-in-policy6}
    edit <policy_number>
        set intf <interface>
        set srcaddr <source_address> [source_address] ...
        set dstaddr <destination_address> [destination_address] ...
        set action {accept | deny}
        set service <service_name> [service_name] ...
        set schedule <schedule_name>
        set comments <string>
    next
end
For example, to prevent the source subnet 10.10.10.0/24 from pinging port1, but allow administrative access for PING on port1:
config firewall address
    edit "10.10.10.0"
        set subnet 10.10.10.0 255.255.255.0
    next
end
config firewall local-in-policy
    edit 1
        set intf "port1"
        set srcaddr "10.10.10.0"
        set dstaddr "all"
        set service "PING"
        set schedule "always"
    next
end

title: Ensure default Admin ports are changed
description: FortiGate admin ports listen on the common ports of 80 and 443. This is default behavior. While interface access is controlled by configuring network interfaces, the FortiGate still listens on the admin ports that have been configured, which can also cause a conflict should 80 or 443 be needed as part of additional configuration later on. FAILs if the HTTP/HTTPS/SSH administrative ports are still the defaults (80, 443, 22); the CIS text uses FortiGate syntax (admin-port/admin-sport), FortiSwitchOS uses system web http-port/https-port. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7.1.1.7 Ensure default Admin ports are changed

remediation.command:
config system global
    set admin-ssh-port 4422
end
config system web
    set http-port 8082
    set https-port 4443
end
# CIS guidance:
config system global
    set admin-https-redirect disable
    set admin-port 8082 **(or any other uncommon port)**
    set admin-server-cert "self-sign"
    set admin-sport 4343 **(or any other uncommon port)**
end
OR From Web GUI:
1. System > Settings
2. Change the ports/settings under 'Administration Settings' section. NOTE: https redirection must be turned off as well as changing port 80. This is due to the nature of how browser port redirection works. The browser will be redirected from port 80 to port 443 or whichever 'admin-sport' is configured, meaning that it will still listen on port 80 even when the port has been reconfigured.

title: VLAN Pruning

audit.command: Note: PortX indicates a numbered port on the FortiSwitch. Example: Port1, port2, port3, etc. From the CLI: show switch interface edit "portX" set allowed-vlans x,x,x From the GUI: 1. Switch > Interfaces > Select portX > Edit 2. Allowed VLANs 3. Ensure that "Allowed VLANs" are specified if the interface is a VLAN tagged interface.

remediation.command:
Note: PortX indicates a numbered port on the FortiSwitch. Example: Port1, port2, port3, etc. From the CLI:

    edit "portX"
        set allowed-vlans x,x,x

From the GUI:

2. Allowed VLANs

title: Change LLDP Profile for All Ports to Default
description: Change LLDP Profile for All Ports to Default FAILs if any physical port still uses the default-auto-isl LLDP profile. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4.1.1 Change LLDP Profile for All Ports to Default

remediation.command:
config switch physical-port
    edit "portX"
        set lldp-profile "default"
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
Note: PortX indicates a numbered port on the FortiSwitch. Example: Port1, port2, port3, etc. From the CLI:

title: DHCP Snooping Enablement
description: DHCP snooping protects the network from common DHCP attacks, including address spoofing resulting from a rogue DHCP server operating on the network or exhaustion of addresses on a DHCP server caused by mass address requests by an attacker on the network. DHCP snooping designates trusted DHCP servers and ports on which DHCP requests and responses are accepted. PASS requires dhcp-snooping enable on at least one VLAN; confirm all user VLANs and trusted uplink ports. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.5.1 DHCP Snooping Enablement

remediation.command:
config switch vlan
    edit <vlan-id>
        set dhcp-snooping enable
    next
end
config switch interface
    edit "<uplink>"
        set dhcp-snooping trusted
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
From the CLI:
config switch vlan
    edit <vlan-id>
        set dhcp-snooping enable
        config dhcp-server-access-list
            edit "DHCP Server"
                set server-ip 192.168.1.1
            end
        end
        config switch interface
            edit "portXX" (XX is the port number.)
                set dhcp-snooping trusted
            end
By default, all ports are untrusted so you will need to specify trusted ports for uplinks to DHCP Servers or to a directly connected DHCP Server. Optionally specify a DHCP server for additional security. From the GUI:
1. Switch > VLAN > Select a VLAN > Edit
2. Under the DHCP Snooping section check the "Enable" checkbox.
3. Optionally, configure a DHCP Server under DHCP Snooping section within the DHCP Server Whitelist configuration.
4. Switch > DHCP Snooping click on button to enable "Only Allow DHCP from Whitelisted Servers".
5. Switch > Interfaces > Select an Interface > Edit
6. Under DHCP Snooping set the uplink and/or the connection to the DHCP Server to "Trusted". By default, all ports are untrusted so you will need to specify trusted ports for uplinks to DHCP Servers or to a directly connected DHCP Server. Optionally specify a DHCP server for additional security.

title: Enable Event Logging
description: Enabling event logging to allow for log generation and review. FAILs if any event type in config log eventfilter is disabled. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.1.1 Enable Event Logging

remediation.command:
config log eventfilter
    set event enable
end
# CIS guidance:
On GUI:
1. Go to Log > Config.
2. Enable "All" Event Logging. On CLI:
config log eventfilter
    set event enable
end

title: Centralized Logging and Reporting
description: Device logs should be sent to a centralized device for log collection, retention, and reporting. This could be a SIEM. syslog device, FortiAnalyzer, FortiManager, etc. PASS requires remote syslog (config log syslogd setting) status enable. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.2.1 Centralized Logging and Reporting

remediation.command:
config log syslogd setting
    set status enable
    set server "10.0.0.50"
end
# CIS guidance:
Configure a remote server for logs to be sent to:
1. Go to Log > Config.
2. Under "Syslog" check the checkbox "Enable", configure a remote server, specify the severity level, and the syslog port.

title: Ensure 'Pre-Login Banner' is set
description: Configure a pre-login banner, ideally approved by the organization's legal team. This banner should, at minimum, prohibit unauthorized access, provide notice of logging or monitoring, and avoid using the word "welcome" or similar words of invitation. PASS requires a non-empty pre-login-banner in config system global. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.2 Ensure 'Pre-Login Banner' is set

remediation.command:
config system global
    set pre-login-banner "Authorized use only. Activity is monitored."
end
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command in the CLI to enable the pre-login-banner:
config system global
    set pre-login-banner <Enter a message for the system pre-login
end

title: Ensure 'Post-Login-Banner' is set
description: Sets the banner after users successfully log in. This is equivalent to Message of the Day (MOTD) in some other systems. PASS requires a non-empty post-login-banner in config system global. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.3 Ensure 'Post-Login-Banner' is set

remediation.command:
config system global
    set post-login-banner "All activity is logged."
end
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command in the CLI to enable the post-login-banner:
config system global
    set post-login-banner <Enter a message for the system post-login
end

title: Ensure DNS server is configured
description: Fortinet uses the Domain Name Service (DNS) to translate host names into IP addresses. To enable DNS lookups, you must specify the primary DNS server for your system. You can also specify secondary and tertiary DNS servers. When resolving host names, the system consults the primary name server. If a failure or time-out occurs, the system consults the secondary name server. For security purpose, trusted DNS servers should be configured to prevent man-in-the- middle attacks. PASS requires a primary DNS server in config system dns. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4.1.1 Ensure DNS server is configured

remediation.command:
config system dns
    set primary 8.8.8.8
    set secondary 8.8.4.4
end
# CIS guidance:
In this example, we will assign 8.8.8.8 as primary DNS and 8.8.4.4 as secondary DNS. In CLI:
config system dns
    set primary 8.8.8.8
    set secondary 8.8.4.4
end
In the GUI, go to System > Network > DNS. Click on "Specify" and put in 8.8.8.8 as "Primary DNS Server" and 8.8.4.4 as "Secondary DNS Server"

title: Enabling SNMP trap for memory usage
description: Enabling SNMP traps for memory usage monitoring helps detect anomalies and ensure critical security features remain operational. This proactive approach enhances system reliability by alerting administrators to potential resource issues. PASS requires an SNMPv3 user whose trap events include mem-low. Audited against FortiSwitchOS 'show full-configuration' output (standalone FortiSwitch, saved in full); patterns are scoped to the named 'config ... end' block, whose member lines are indented.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5.1.4 Enabling SNMP trap for memory usage

remediation.command:
config system snmp user
    edit "<user>"
        set events cpu-high mem-low log-full intf-ip ent-conf-change llv
    next
end
# CIS guidance:
To configure SNMPv3 trap "mem-low" in addition to all trap "Events". From CLI:
config system snmp user
    show
    config system snmp user
        set events cpu-high mem-low log-full intf-ip ent-conf-change llv
    end

title: Ensure hostname is set

remediation.command:
config system global
    set hostname "FSW-IDF1-01"
end
# CIS guidance:
In CLI, set the hostname to 'New_FSW1' as follows:

    set hostname "New_FSW1"
end
In GUI
1) Go to 'System' > 'Config' > 'Hostname'
2) Update the field 'New Hostname' with the new hostname

title: Ensure timezone is properly configured
description: Sets the local time zone information so that the time displayed by the device is more relevant to those who are viewing it.
reference: CIS FortiSwitch Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5.4.2 Ensure timezone is properly configured

audit.command: In the CLI, do the following command and check the result of timezone filed in the output get system global | grep timezone timezone : (GMT-8:00) Pacific Time (US & Canada) Or from GUI, do the following: 1) Login to FortiSwitch 2) Go to 'System' -> 'Config' -> 'Time' 3) TimeZone and NTP settings are under 'System Time'

remediation.command:
In this example, we will set Eastern Timezone (GMT-5:00) for the FortiSwitch. Each timezone will have its corresponding ID. To find the correct ID, when you type in the command "set timezone ", also type the question mark '?' to list all of the available timezones and their IDs. The ID of the Eastern Timezone is 12 In the CLI:
config system global
    set timezone 12
end
In the GUI, do the following:
1) After login to FortiSwich, go to 'System' -> 'Config' -> 'Time'
2) Select '12 - (GMT-5:00) Eastern Time (US & Canada)' under 'System Time' -> 'TimeZone'
